title: How does a Personal Checking owner opt in or out of overdraft for ATM and debit card transactions?
content:
## Scope

This policy governs the debit overdraft election on a Personal Checking account: the owner's choice of whether ATM withdrawals and one-time debit card purchases may be paid into overdraft.

## Formal clauses

1. **What the election governs.** The debit overdraft election governs only ATM withdrawals and one-time debit card purchases. Checks, ACH debits and recurring debit card payments are unaffected by it.
2. **Opting in needs the owner's own consent.** Opting in requires the owner's own affirmative consent, given by the owner rather than recorded on the owner's behalf.
3. **Opting in needs a tier with coverage.** Opting in is available only on a tier that offers discretionary overdraft coverage, as shown by the account's tier.
4. **Opting out.** Opting out can be requested at any time on any tier and takes effect when recorded.
5. **No retroactive effect.** A new election applies to transactions authorized after it is recorded and never re-prices items already paid or declined. An opt-out does not refund fees already assessed.
6. **Same election again.** Recording the election already in force changes nothing and records nothing.

## Request table

| Request | Tier offers coverage | Owner's own affirmative consent given | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opt in | Yes | Yes | The opt-in may be recorded |
| Opt in | Yes | No (for example, someone else asks on the owner's behalf) | Not recorded |
| Opt in | No | — | Not available on this tier |
| Opt out | Any tier | — | Recorded; effective when recorded |
| Same election as the one in force | Any tier | — | Nothing changes and nothing is recorded |

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

- **Timing.** An owner opts out at 10:00 on a given day. A one-time debit card purchase authorized at 09:30 that day was authorized before the opt-out was recorded, so the new election does not re-price it; a purchase authorized at 11:00 falls under the opt-out.
- **Fees already charged.** An owner who paid an overdraft fee on a card purchase last week opts out today. The opt-out does not refund that fee.
- **Tier without coverage.** An owner whose tier does not offer discretionary overdraft coverage asks to opt in. The opt-in is not available on that tier; opting out remains available.

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** "opting out stops checks from being paid into overdraft". **Correct basis:** checks, ACH debits and recurring debit card payments are unaffected by the election.
